subject: Rapid notification playbook — subprocessor geo-exceptions & evidence handoff
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Sanders <julie.sanders@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Rapid notification playbook — subprocessor geo-exceptions & evidence handoff

Julie / Finex security team,

Following our call this morning, I wanted to put a short, actionable plan on paper so we can align on timelines and evidence scope. High level: we can support a staged notification + limited evidence handoff for affected accounts, but need to confirm subprocessor geography and the exact artifacts you require.

Key asks from our side (so we can commit to timelines):
- Confirm whether the affected tenant(s) include EU-resident data (GDPR scope).
- Confirm the primary point(s) of contact for forensic access (one security, one legal).
- Let us know whether you require export of full forensic snapshots or only redacted metadata (we can do both but export window and approvals differ).

Our proposed mutual action plan (we can adjust):
1) Acknowledgement to customer and Finex legal within 36 hours (we can do 24 if urgent).
2) Containment summary and high-level scope to be shared within 48 hours.
3) Forensic snapshot availability (read-only) within 72 hours if approved via secure transfer; full export subject to legal approval and DPA carveouts.
4) If EU data present, we will route export through our EU-controlled subprocessor path; otherwise we can use standard SFTP escrow (details below).

Attachments: proposed-rapid-notify-playbook.pdf (playbook draft), subprocessor-inventory-2026-12.csv (redacted list).

If you can reply with the POC names and whether you want a full snapshot or redacted artifacts, we’ll start the internal approvals and kick off the SFTP prep.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

---
Attachment stubs: proposed-rapid-notify-playbook.pdf (PDF, 12 pages); subprocessor-inventory-2026-12.csv (CSV, redacted).

From: Julie Sanders <julie.sanders@finexcorp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@finexcorp.com, legal+procurement@finexcorp.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rapid notification playbook — subprocessor geo-exceptions & evidence handoff

Naomi,

Thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers up front:
- Finex affected tenant MAY include EU-resident records; we are confirming with Product and will know within 6 hours.
- POCs: me (Julie Sanders, Security Lead) and Mark Runnels (Finex Legal) copied on follow-ups.
- For initial triage we need: timeline-stamped access logs (SAML + API tokens), object-level change history, and KV-cache dump for the 24h window around the suspected event.

Two immediate clarifications from our legal team before we proceed:
1) Under our DPA, Finex requires evidence exports of EU personal data to be via an EU-controlled export path (HSM/KMS-bound) — can Redwood provide an EU-bound encrypt-at-rest transfer and attest to KMS controls?
2) If evidence includes third-party subprocessor data, procurement requires a subprocessor attestation and list for the last 12 months.

We’re happy to accept a redacted snapshot first to unblock triage while legal reviews export requests. Please confirm how Redwood will redact PII and whether you’ll provide a notarized chain-of-custody manifest.

Julie
Julie Sanders
Security Lead, FinexCorp
julie.sanders@finexcorp.com

---
Reply includes request for SAML logs and a notarized chain-of-custody.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Julie Sanders <julie.sanders@finexcorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Rapid notification playbook — subprocessor geo-exceptions & evidence handoff

Julie —

Appreciate the quick turn. Short answers and proposed confirmations:

1) EU-controlled export: we can stage evidence in our EU vault (Amsterdam region) and provide a KMS-backed export. The export will be AES-256 encrypted and the KMS key will be EU-resident; we will provide the key wrapping attestation and KMS metadata. This satisfies our standard DPA carveouts for cross-border evidence transfers.

2) Subprocessor attestation: attached is the redacted subprocessor inventory (subprocessor-inventory-2026-12.csv). If you need the full historic attestation package, we can produce it under an NDA supplement; procurement typically requests the 12-month appendix which we can deliver in 48 hours.

3) Redaction approach & chain of custody: for initial triage we will produce a redacted snapshot that strips direct PII fields (email, phone, SSNs) and replaces identifiers with one-way hashed tokens. We will include a chain-of-custody manifest (signed by our legal ops) and a hash digest of the exported tarball. If you want notarization, we can route through our partner notarization service (extra step, +24–48h).

Proposed next steps:
- Please confirm whether you want the EU-vault export or an interim redacted SFTP snapshot.
- If EU, provide written approval from Finex legal to proceed and we’ll open a DocuSign approval link (we’ll attach the narrow export authorization).
- If redacted SFTP, confirm SFTP endpoint details (we can provide temporary creds and an SFTP fingerprint).

I’ll loop in our ops team after you confirm (Ben + Kimberly on cc).

Naomi
---
Attachment: subprocessor-inventory-2026-12.csv (CSV, partial redaction).
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-finex-evidence (read-only request link).

Subject: Re: Rapid notification playbook — subprocessor geo-exceptions & evidence handoff

Internal — quick ops note before we finalize the DocuSign flow:

- Ops can spin the EU KMS-wrapped snapshot in ~18 hours once legal approval is in place. We will not export private KMS keys; export will be an encrypted artifact with KMS metadata.
- For SFTP transfers we should push a one-time password + IP-egress restriction. Put Vanessa on the access liaison in case we need to coordinate the notarization partner.
- If procurement wants the 12-month subproc attestation, route that request to Legal Ops (I can PR the package; Kimberly can confirm redaction scope).

Naomi — I’ll draft the narrow export approval language for DocuSign and circulate tonight.

Ben Carter
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
